newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chinese diesel prices recover, imports subdued.
newsitem.headline: Chinese diesel prices recover, imports subdued.

text.p: China is unlikely to initiate large diesel imports immediately even though the local refineries are seeing improved sales, higher prices and a fall in stocks, refining sources and traders said on Thursday.

Domestic diesel prices have increased by between $20 and $30 per tonne after the government's latest measures to curb illicit imports by foreign-invested firms, which forced them to buy from Chinese refineries, the sources said.
"Last month we could not even sell at 1,900 yuan (US$229) per tonne. We are selling at 2,070 yuan (US$249) this week," said a source with Fujian Refinery and Chemical Co.

China's state-set, ex-refinery diesel price stands at 2,190 yuan (US$263) per tonne but many coastal refineries were forced to cut their prices to compete with oil smugglers who brought in diesel without paying taxes.

Apart from smuggling, many foreign-invested firms, which are allowed to import low-tariffed diesel for their own use, sold their oil in the domestic markets for a profit, putting more downward pressure on diesel prices.
Beijing started in late June to curb imports by foreign-invested firms and the move has largely boosted sales at Chinese refineries, Chinese traders said.
"Our diesel stocks are still high but we should be able to see more sales in the near term," the Fujian refinery source said by telephone.
Sources at coastal Guangdong and Maoming refineries said the two refineries were selling diesel at "almost the same" levels set by the state, also noting improving diesel sales.

Despite increasing sales of stocked diesel, Chinese sources said it was unlikely to see fresh demand from China, dismissing speculation in the Singapore market that Chinese buying would soon emerge after the prolonged absence.

"There is no plan to import diesel soon. The current diesel stocks can meet domestic demand for two month or so," a source at China's state importer, China National Chemicals Import and Export (SINOCHEM), said from Beijing.

The source said even after diesel stocks levels have fallen, the Chinese refineries would boost their diesel production by importing more gas oil rich-crude oil rather than initiate a new round of imports.
This is in line with the state policy of producing more oil products domestically, they said.

"We have enough diesel stocks and the government has not issued new import licences recently. We have no plan to import diesel any time soon and I don't think other refineries will," the Fujian refinery source said.
